title: Cap. XIV: Editor exhibits Placeus MS vs Garissoles shreds — before Manuscriptum posterius
pass_a_gloss: Wherefore nothing seems to me more advisable than that I exhibit that manuscript of Placeus to you, Reader (For why would I put my labor either in proposing or in refuting those arguments, when that has already been performed by Placeus himself?) and, when D. Garissoles wished to refute it, and transcribed its scraps and patches passim into his own book, and as far as he could confuted it, I will subjoin to each of those particles that man's censures, and to these very ones Placeus's defenses. So you will be able, most equitable Reader, quite easily, and without the hazard of erring, to know this whole cause and to give judgment: which otherwise would be difficult, not to say impossible. For scarcely can it be well discerned with what mind, in what sense, each thing was said, when only torn parts of the discourse, torn from their places and as it were dislocated and scattered, are offered to the reader. Nor is there reason that anyone should take offense on that account. For if anything in that writing is worthy of censure, it is to be thought to have place especially in those parts which have already been published by D. Garissoles. It had indeed not been composed by Placeus with the design that it should be edited, and from too great haste perhaps some things crept in which, if leisure had been allowed the author, were to be emended and polished: yet we have wished not even to remove, add, or change a little word, lest anyone be able to complain of our faith or sincerity. Whatever it is, you, most equitable Reader, will take it in good part, and because we give you the opportunity of reading it whole and of judging this whole controversy, you will either thank us, or at least bear it with no unfair mind.
pass_b_english: Nothing therefore seems wiser than to set that Placeus manuscript before you, Reader (why should I spend myself proposing or answering those arguments when Placeus has already done it?), and, since Garissoles chose to refute it and copied its scraps and patches into his own book and answered them as he could, to set under each scrap that man's censures and Placeus's own defenses. So you, most fair Reader, may know the whole cause easily and without risk of error, and judge—which would otherwise be hard, not to say impossible. One can scarcely see with what mind or sense each thing was said when only torn, uprooted, and scattered pieces of the discourse are offered. Let no one take offense at that. If anything in the writing deserves blame, it is chiefly in the parts Garissoles has already published. Placeus did not compose it to be printed, and haste may have left spots he would have polished at leisure; yet we would not drop, add, or change even a word, lest anyone doubt our honesty. Take it, most fair Reader, in good part: we give you the whole to read and the whole controversy to judge—thank us, or at least bear it without ill will.
source_text: Quare nihil mihi videtur consultius, quam ut manuscriptum illud Placei tibi, Lector, exhibeam (Cur enim in illis argumentis vel proponendis, vel refutandis operam meam ponerem, cum id jam fuerit ab ipso Placeo praestitum?) ac, quando id refutare voluit D. Garissolius, ejusque passim frustula et lacinias transcripsit in suum librum, et quantum potuit, confutavit, subjiciam singulis illis particulis viri illius reprehensiones, hisque ipsis Placei defensiones. Ita poteris, Lector aequissime, admodum facile, et citra errandi aleam, de tota hac causa cognoscere, et judicium ferre: id quod alioqui difficile, ne dicam impossibile, foret. Vix enim qua mente, quo sensu quidque dictum fuerit, bene perspici potest, cum lacerae tantum, et suis locis revulsae, ac veluti luxatae et dissipatae partes sermonis legenti offeruntur. Neque est quod quisquam propterea offendatur. Si quid enim in eo scripto reprehensione dignum est, id in iis potissimum partibus habere locum putandum est, quae jam sunt a D. Garissolio vulgatae. Non eo quidem consilio a Placeo compositum fuerat ut ederetur, et ex nimia festinatione irrepsere fortasse nonnulla, si per otium licuisset autori, emendanda atque expolienda: tamen ne voculam quidem tollere, addere, aut mutare voluimus, ne quis de nostra fide vel synceritate conqueri posset. Qualecunque est, Tu aequissime Lector, illud aequi bonique consules, quodque ejus integri legendi, totiusque istius controversiae dijudicandae copiam tibi facimus, aut habebis nobis gratiam, aut saltem non iniquo animo feres.
